  • Strong hire: separates host and share receiver, persists state, covers trampoline limits, test matrix, rollout and rollback.

questions.contextHtml: A travel app (4M DAU, 60% on Android 13+) has 9 activities overriding onBackPressed(), 14 fragments with custom Back logic, three third-party SDK activities, and a custom dispatchKeyEvent in a base class that intercepts KEYCODE_BACK for analytics. Product wants predictive back animations before targeting API 36. Last attempt to flip enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" on the application in a beta caused: payment confirmation dialog not showing (0.8% of payment attempts failed to confirm in the beta cohort of 20K), Back doing nothing in a map screen, and an analytics drop of Back events by 100%. Release train is every 2 weeks; you cannot pause features.
questions.promptHtml: Plan the migration without hurting live users.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Replace all onBackPressed with callbacks and flip the flag." Big-bang, unverifiable, and ignores SDK activities and the analytics hook.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Which screens are money-critical? Can SDK activities be opted out? What is the min compat level of androidx.activity? Are there Fragments using show/hide or custom stacks? Is there a staged rollout/feature flag infra?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Keep the flag off in production; revert the beta change. Nothing user-facing is blocked: predictive back is an enhancement until target 36.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked (what broke): (a) onBackPressed overrides are never called after opt-in; (b) dispatchKeyEvent Back interception is bypassed; (c) callbacks registered but disabled in a way that lets the system animate then finish; (d) SDK activities with their own handling (they may keep legacy behavior per activity).
  4. How I'd verify each: grep for onBackPressed, KEYCODE_BACK, onKeyDown; instrumentation tests using pressBack(); manual test with Developer options predictive back; log which callbacks are enabled.
  5. Root cause: back logic was imperative and distributed; the system now needs declarative, pre-registered callbacks.
  6. Fix (plan):
    • Phase 0: upgrade androidx.activity / fragment / Navigation to versions supporting the back-event APIs (activity 1.6+, fragment 1.6+; verify exact versions).
    • Phase 1 (no flag): convert each onBackPressed into an OnBackPressedCallback with state-driven isEnabled; these work with the flag off too. Move analytics to a callback or a dispatcher wrapper.
    • Phase 2: set enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" per activity, starting with simple screens, with a remote kill-switch for the manifest-independent code paths (the manifest itself is not remotely switchable; ship per-activity opt-in over several releases and use staged rollout percentages for each).
    • Phase 3: payment and map screens last, with extra tests and a canary cohort.
    • Phase 4: bump targetSdk to 36 after everything passes; keep the SDK activities updated or isolated.
<activity android:name=".SettingsActivity" android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" />
  1. Prevention: lint/grep CI check banning onBackPressed overrides; test base class; checklist entry for new screens.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not opt in at the application level first; I would not wrap KEYCODE_BACK as a workaround; I accept a slower rollout in exchange for protecting payments.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Third-party SDK activity ignores callbacks? → Opt it out at activity level if allowed, update the SDK, or isolate behind a wrapper; verify target-36 behavior.
  • Do dialogs get predictive back? → Standard dialogs register their own callback; custom views need explicit callbacks.
  • How do you measure success? → Back-related crash/ANR, payment confirmation rate, user complaints, and animation adoption.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A migration was derailed by one base activity that swallowed Back for analytics; once the analytics was moved to a lifecycle-aware observer, 80% of screens needed no code changes.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: flips the flag everywhere.
  • Hire: phased per-activity opt-in with callbacks and tests.
  • Strong hire: handles SDKs, analytics hook, payment risk, targetSdk sequencing, rollout metrics and rollback.

questions.contextHtml: After a new release, support gets reports that "the app opens twice": after installing from the store and tapping Open, then pressing Home and tapping the launcher icon, users see a second copy of the splash/login screen, and pressing Back shows the first one. Crash-free rate is 99.7%, nothing in logs. It reproduces on 8% of installs, mostly through sideloaded APKs and some OEM installers, rarely from Play. SplashActivity is the launcher activity and launchMode is standard. Product notes: "we turned on Android 12 root-back last week", which is likely unrelated.
questions.promptHtml: Explain the mechanism, fix it, and say how you would validate.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Make Splash singleTask." This hides the symptom but changes behavior of every launch (and deep links), and does not explain the cause.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Does it reproduce after install-and-Open only? Which installers (package installer, OEM store)? Do both instances show the same task id in dumpsys? Are the flags on the two launches different (Open from installer vs launcher icon)?
  2. Immediate mitigation: A guard in SplashActivity.onCreate: if it is not the task root and was launched from the launcher, finish immediately.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) the installer starts the launcher activity with different flags/task (a new task not marked as the app's normal launch), so the launcher icon later starts another instance in another task (known historic behavior around Open-after-install); (b) a deep link or notification starts Splash with NEW_TASK; (c) Android 12 root back behavior (red herring); (d) process restart.
  4. How I'd verify each: Install via adb install and via the OEM store, launch, press Home, tap the icon; run adb shell dumpsys activity activities to compare the two task records and their intents (flags, affinity, root intent). Log intent.flags and isTaskRoot.
  5. Root cause: The installer's "Open" launch and the launcher icon launch create tasks that the system does not consider the same, so a second Splash instance starts; this has been seen with some installers historically, and exact behavior varies by OEM and release; I would confirm on the affected devices rather than assume.
  6. Fix: classic guard:
override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    if (!isTaskRoot &&
        intent.hasCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_LAUNCHER) &&
        intent.action == Intent.ACTION_MAIN) {
        finish(); return
    }
    // normal splash
}

Long-term: use the AndroidX SplashScreen API (core-splashscreen) so the splash is not a separate activity; move launch routing into the host activity. 7. Prevention: QA matrix includes install-and-open from non-Play installers; a startup test that asserts a single task for the app after relaunch. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not change launchMode to singleTask for this; I would not leave the guard permanently if the AndroidX Splash migration removes the condition (remove dead code); be wary that finish() in onCreate shows a brief flicker on some OEMs.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Why not FLAG_ACTIVITY_BROUGHT_TO_FRONT check? → That is the variant of the same guard used in older answers; use isTaskRoot plus the MAIN/LAUNCHER check.
  • Will Play-installed users be affected? → Rarely; verify with install-referrer segmentation.
  • Does the guard break Direct launches with extras? → It only acts when not root and launched as MAIN/LAUNCHER.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A subtle second-instance bug only appeared in a QA lab using a custom installer; we reproduced it with adb by starting the same launcher intent with and without --activity-new-task, and a six-line guard closed it.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: changes launchMode without evidence.
  • Hire: reproduces, compares tasks via dumpsys, applies isTaskRoot guard.
  • Strong hire: explains task identity mechanism with honest uncertainty, adds test matrix, and plans removal via the Splash API migration.
